slides.texte_overlay:
habits that give you a
bold kind of confidence

volunteering to speak

in the next group project, be the one who says i'll present. the nerves last two minutes, but the respect you quietly earn from it lasts the whole year.

praising others out loud

this week, praise someone who did good work, out loud and in front of others. people who praise freely are the ones everyone naturally sees as leaders.

asking a real question

once a week, ask your boss or teacher a real question about how they think, not about the task. most people never do, and it makes you truly memorable.

a coffee break fact

use one coffee break a day to learn something new in 5 minutes, a short history or science fact. having one interesting thing to share makes speaking up so much easier.

use one coffee break a day to learn something new. the Sophia app turns it into one short lesson, a history or science fact, and you always have something smart to share.

keeping your word

say clearly when you'll finish something, then finish a little early. every promise you keep adds a little more weight to your quiet, steady confidence.
